rule: A behaviour-frontier counter above its target names who retires it or the gate prints that nobody does. Counter 4's creditor is a campaign stage and resolves through docs/receipts/campaign-stages.json; counters 1-3 have no stage, because they were met from the day the instrument was written and owed nobody until the e201490d..origin/main merge brought a kernel that had never been measured against them. Exactly one row may claim a debt -- behavior_frontier.debt_owner raises on two -- and a row leaves this file on the commit that drives its counter to its target, never before.

debts.cause: Counter 1 was 0 on this branch: every item behaviour resolved through item_effects/item_behavior_catalog rather than through a name. main's arriving modules dispatch on the item name again -- cleanse_eligibility's CLEANSE_ACTIVE_SOURCES (9) and ITEM_CLEANSE_DECLARATIONS (11) key the cleanse vocabulary by name, item_support_effects names 16 support producers plus _FIMBULWINTER_TRIGGER_RULE, interaction_effects' _ANNUL_ITEM_NAMES names 3, damage.py names 22 at their call sites, and pipeline.py names 1. Each is a real behaviour this branch did not model, so none of them is deleted here: the debt is to move the dispatch onto a declared registry key, which is the same act criterion 1 always named.
debts.follow_up: One slice per module, in the order the counts run: cleanse_eligibility first (its 20 are one vocabulary and the F-9 follow-up already opens it -- KNOWN_CONTROL_KINDS and CC_KIND_VOCABULARY disagree), then item_support_effects' 17, then damage.py's 22, then the 4 singletons. Each slice moves the counter, regenerates docs/behavior-frontier.json in its own commit (R-36), and edits this row's measured value or removes the row.
